title: Invoke Toolchain Oddities — scratch log
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad capturing the chain of commands, partial outputs, and hypotheses while tracking a weird behavior in tool/function calling + structured output parsing. Not polished — for my own timeline and to hand off to Marco if needed.

Symptoms observed (overview):
- Intermittent partial JSON returned in function call payloads when responses stream and the response crosses a token boundary.
- Sometimes the call name in the metadata (function_to_call) is correct but the arguments object is truncated (trailing comma or missing closing brace).
- Failures happen more when a long list is emitted from the model (array of items) or during retry after a transient kernel fallback.

Relevant timestamps and quick repro identifiers:
- 2026-02-15 09:23 PST: First user report (internal test app) — saw "{"items": [ ... " then stream dropped and client tried to parse -> JSON error.
- 2026-02-16 14:07 PST: Reproduced on local desktop with small prompt that encourages long array output.
- Repro tag: INF-2247-REPRO-A (attached to Linear ticket above).

Commands / experiments run (log):
1) Basic curl replicate (streaming):
   curl -sS -N -X POST https://api.redwood.local/v1/generate \
     -H 'Authorization: Bearer dev-token' \
     -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
     -d '{"model":"rwd-small-2026","prompt":"generate 120 short JSON objects as an array","max_tokens":800,"stream":true,"function_call":{"name":"ingestList","arguments_schema":{"type":"object","properties":{"items":{"type":"array"}}}}}'
   --> Observed: stream includes function call start frame with arguments payload that ends mid-array (no closing ] or }). Client JSON.parse fails.

2) Python SDK (sync non-stream):
   from redwood import Client
   c = Client(token=...)
   res = c.generate(model='rwd-small-2026', prompt='generate 120 short JSON objects as an array', max_tokens=800, function_call={'name':'ingestList'})
   --> Observed: complete arguments present (server returned composed non-streamed frame). Suggests streaming path has a bug in chunk framing.

3) Local dev mode with logging enabled (runtime serve --log-framing=debug):
   - Saw chunk boundary at kernel fallback moment (gpu-1 -> cpu fallback). Last chunk flagged as 'partial=true', and next chunk had 'partial=false' but missing the finishing bytes.
   - Hypothesis: the stream aggregator that builds the function call payload isn't atomically concatenating frames when fallback occurs. Race between flush and fallback cleanup.

4) Forced small chunk sizes by lowering stream buffer in runtime: set env STREAM_CHUNK_BYTES=128 and re-run.
   - Result: more frequent truncations (expected) but parsing failures show same symptom (final chunk missing trailing braces).

5) Attempted client-side tolerant parse: replace trailing ',' with ']' heuristics and attempt JSON5 parse.
   - Temporary mitigation: in client, if parse fails and last received chunk ends with ',' or '"', try append 'null]' or ']' to close. Works for a subset but not reliable. Also dangerous in production.

Error snippets (copied raw):
- Parser error: "Unexpected end of JSON input at position 5432"
- Last stream chunk (hex preview): 7b 22 69 74 65 6d 73 22 3a 20 5b 7b 22 69 64 22 3a 20 22 31 22 7d 2c 7b 22 69 64 22 3a 20 22 32 22 7d 2c 7b 22 69 64 22 3a 20 22 33 22 7d 2c 7b 22 69 64 22 3a 20 22 34 22 7d 2c 7b 22 69 64 22 3a 20 22 35 22 7d 2c 0a\n  (ends with 0a newline, no closing ] or })

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Streaming frame aggregator bug: when runtime switches execution paths (e.g., due to fallback or kernel selection), the buffered last frame gets dropped or an abort path runs that doesn't flush closing tokens. (high)
2) Tokenizer / detokenizer mismatch between kernel variants: one kernel produces a special internal tokenizer sequence for end-of-args that the aggregator doesn't recognize, so it's not appended. (medium)
3) Client library mishandling of final stream event: if the stream ends with a keepalive and the client treats it as closure without waiting for final 'done' frame. (low — ruled out by server-side logs where aggregator didn't include final bytes)
4) Model output variability: model answered with a trailing comma and newline and we fail to sanitize. (low — model sometimes outputs valid JSON in non-stream path)

Quick notes on where the data indicates the bug lives:
- Non-stream responses are intact -> server assembles final payload correctly in non-stream codepath.
- Server debug logs show a call to aggregator.append(frame) followed immediately by aggregator.rollback() in fallback case -> code smell.
- Rollback path does not attempt to re-emit buffered suffix tokens.

Minimal repro plan (next actions):
- Make a deterministic small test that forces fallback: use a custom injected kernel error after N tokens to simulate fallback. Script will run multiple times and check final stream payload.
- Add server-side assertion: if any frame has partial=true and next frame is absent after X ms, emit trace to S3 with sequence of frames and kernel ids.
- Add test harness that compares streamed concatenation against non-stream assembly for same seed / prompt.

Temporary mitigations (for customer-facing):
- Client SDK: implement a safe recovery try — if parse fails on function-call args, re-request non-stream (fast retry) with warn-level telemetry. This avoids having to attempt heuristic fixes.
- Server-side: short-term, ensure fallback path calls flush_buffer(true) to force append of pending suffix before abort. (low-risk change to try)

Notes to hand off to Marco:
- See PR 987 for the aggregator refactor that touched fallback logic. Suspect the recent patch missed a codepath.
- I will attach raw frame dumps (S3) from next repro runs. Could use your help writing the deterministic kernel-fail test harness.

Thoughts about long-term:
- We should formalize "atomic framing" for function-call arguments: ensure that frames that start an object are either delivered in full or the server emits a clear error frame (so client does not attempt to parse).
- Add a streaming contract doc: define partial/complete markers for function call payloads (explicit end-of-arguments token framed separately).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Can we add a small signature/footer token for function-call payloads so clients can detect truncation? (tradeoff: extra bytes on every call)
- Who owns the fallback path in the runtime team — platform-engineering or serving-runtime? I think serving-runtime but need confirmation (ask @Priya).

Immediate next steps (my plan):
- 2026-03-13: write deterministic kernel-fail harness (local) and run 100 iterations, attach dumps.
- 2026-03-14: prototype server change flush_buffer(true) in fallback and run same harness.
- If repro rate > 80% -> roll small patch to staging and enable enhanced logging for production streams (sampled).

Scratch TODO (commands I will run locally):
- python tools/stream_repro.py --model rwd-small-2026 --seed 42 --force-fallback-after 320
- curl ... (stream) -> pipe to file and run python scripts/stream_hex_diff.py file1 file2

Last notes:
- This is annoying because the symptom is a hard parse error and surfaces in product as "malformed response" which is high-severity in the SDK. Need to get a reliable trace chain before shipping any bandaid.
- Keep this doc as the working timeline; I'll convert to a PR description once we have deterministic repro/dumps.

-- Aisha
